quote: Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 1) with zero angle on the bow. Submerged when range closed to 8 miles.
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 2) with zero angle on the bow. Submerged when range closed to 8 miles.
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 4) distance 12 miles. Submerged.
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 5) banking to come in on port quarter. ... Submerged; conducting submerged patrol.
8-9 November: Patrolling track prescribed by task group commander. Submerged during daylight. (routine applies until 1944-11-09)
Detected radar interference on 157 mcs. on APR ... Believed this to be aircraft radar so at 1920 Submerged.
Surfaced. Same radar interference soon steady on us.
Surfaced. ... this was probably shore based radar and not plane radar
Submerged. Effective patrol impossible in state 7-8 seas
Spent most of the day at 150 feet. Several attempts to come up to periscope depth were unsuccessful.
Surfaced. Low visibility and state 4 sea made periscope patrol ineffective.
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 6) distance 7 miles. Submerged.
16-17 November: Patrolled submerged during daylight. (routine applies until 1944-11-17)
Sighted red rocket from direction of convoy and immediately afterwards heard depth charging.

Subsequent to each attack and between attacks there was much depth charging gunfire and signalling but none of it was directed specifically at us. (all seven attacks were made on the surface; time approximate)
Submerged at position of first attack.
Surfaced. Thought perhaps sampan had picked up some survivors
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 12) distance 10 miles. Submerged. Continued search submerged for the rest of the day
Surfaced and set course for Pearl.
Sighted plane (Plane Contact No. 13) distance 15 miles with zero angle on the bow. Submerged when range closed to 8 miles.
